title: Votes and seats in the 1952 Lok Sabha election
body: In the 1952 Lok Sabha election, the Congress obtained about 45 per cent of the total votes, but it won 364 of the 489 seats, that is, about 74 per cent of the seats. The Socialist Party, the second largest party in terms of votes, secured more than 10 per cent of the votes all over the country, but it could not win even 3 per cent of the seats. The Communist Party of India, which came second in terms of seats, won 16 seats. If the votes of all the non-Congress candidates were added together, they were more than the votes of the Congress. But the non-Congress votes were divided between different rival parties and candidates, so the Congress was still way ahead of the opposition in most constituencies and managed to win.
